def: Any information relating to a living person who can be identified from it, directly or indirectly.

formal.ex: The Company processes [[personal data]] relating to its employees for the purposes set out in this notice.

everyday.ex: HR already holds your [[personal details]], so you won't need to fill the form in again.
everyday.ex_us: HR already has your [[personal information]], so you won't need to fill out the form again.

collocations: to hold personal data on someone
note_fr: « Data » est aujourd'hui traité comme un indénombrable singulier : « the data is stored », jamais « a data » ni « datas ». Aux États-Unis, on parle plutôt de « personal information » ou de « PII » ; « personal data » y est compris mais sonne européen.

def: The body of rules governing how organisations collect, use, store and share information about individuals.

formal.ex: The parties shall comply with all applicable [[data protection legislation]].
formal.ex_us: The parties shall comply with all applicable [[data privacy laws]].

everyday.ex: Have you run this past whoever looks after [[data protection]]?
everyday.ex_us: Have you run this by whoever handles [[privacy]]?

collocations: to raise a data protection concern
note_fr: « Data protection » est le terme européen et britannique ; les Américains disent « privacy » ou « data privacy ». Prononciation : /ˈdeɪtə/ partout ; /ˈdætə/ s'entend surtout aux États-Unis, /ˈdɑːtə/ est rare.

fr: RGPD (règlement général sur la protection des données)
def: The European Union regulation that sets the rules for processing personal data; the United Kingdom has kept its own version of it.

formal.ex: This policy has been drawn up in accordance with [[the General Data Protection Regulation]].

everyday.ex: Is that actually a [[GDPR]] requirement, or just something IT would like?

note_fr: Ne dites jamais « RGPD » à un anglophone : le sigle est GDPR, épelé lettre par lettre. Le Royaume-Uni applique depuis le Brexit le « UK GDPR », complété par sa propre loi sur la protection des données ; les États-Unis n'ont pas de texte fédéral équivalent.

def: To carry out any operation on personal data, from collecting and storing it to sharing or deleting it.

formal.ex: The Employer shall [[process]] the Employee's data only for purposes connected with the employment relationship.

everyday.ex: Only the payroll team should be [[handling]] salary information.

collocations: to process data on behalf of someone
note_fr: « Traitement » se dit « processing » (indénombrable) : « un traitement » = « a processing activity » ou « a processing operation », pas « a treatment ». Le simple fait de conserver un dossier est déjà un « processing ».

def: The person whom a piece of personal data is about.

formal.ex: Each [[data subject]] shall be informed of the purposes for which his or her data is processed.

everyday.ex: We can't hand that over without asking [[the person concerned]] first.
everyday.ex_us: We can't hand that over without asking [[the individual]] first.

collocations: a request from a data subject
note_fr: « Data subject » est un terme de juriste : devant des salariés ou des managers, dites « the individual », « the employee » ou « the person concerned ». Attention au calque « the concerned person », qui signifie « la personne inquiète ».

def: The organisation that decides why and how personal data is processed, and that is answerable for it.

formal.ex: The Employer acts as [[the controller]] of the personal data described in this notice.

everyday.uk: to be responsible for the data
everyday.us: to be responsible for the data
everyday.ex: As the employer, you're the one who's [[responsible for the data]], even if a provider runs the system.

note_fr: Ne traduisez pas par « responsible of treatment » ni « data manager ». L'employeur est presque toujours « controller » des données de ses salariés. Aux États-Unis, les lois d'État emploient soit « controller », soit « business » (Californie).

def: An organisation that processes personal data on behalf of the controller and on its instructions, such as a payroll provider.

formal.ex: [[The processor]] shall act only on the documented instructions of the controller.

everyday.ex: Payroll is run by an [[outside provider]], so they see everyone's bank details.
everyday.ex_us: Payroll is run by an [[outside vendor]], so they see everyone's bank information.

collocations: to act on the controller's instructions
note_fr: Faux ami majeur : le « sous-traitant » du RGPD est un « processor », pas un « subcontractor » (qui désigne le sous-traitant d'un marché). Le sous-traitant de second rang se dit « sub-processor ».

def: A document telling individuals what data is collected about them, why, for how long, and what their rights are.

formal.ex: A copy of the employee [[privacy notice]] is provided to every new starter on or before the first day of employment.

everyday.ex: It's all in the [[privacy notice]] you were given when you joined.

note_fr: « Privacy » se prononce /ˈprɪvəsi/ au Royaume-Uni et /ˈpraɪvəsi/ aux États-Unis. « Privacy notice » informe les personnes ; « privacy policy » désigne plutôt, en interne, les règles que l'entreprise s'impose - mais les deux sont souvent confondus, surtout sur les sites web.

def: Agreement to the use of one's data that is given without pressure and can be refused without any adverse consequence.

formal.ex: Consent cannot be regarded as [[freely given]] where the employee has no genuine choice.

everyday.ex: If they can't really say no to their boss, it isn't [[a genuine choice]].

note_fr: Point clé pour les clients américains : en Europe, le consentement d'un salarié est rarement valable, à cause du lien de subordination (« imbalance of power »). On s'appuie sur une autre base légale. Aux États-Unis, à l'inverse, faire signer un « consent form » reste le réflexe habituel.

def: To take back an agreement previously given to the use of one's data.

formal.ex: You may [[withdraw your consent]] at any time by writing to the HR department.

everyday.ex: You're free to [[change your mind]] about the photo at any point, and we'll take it down.

informal.ex: A couple of people have [[opted out]] of the staff directory photos.

collocations: to withdraw consent at any time
note_fr: « Retirer » = « withdraw » (withdrew, withdrawn), pas « retire » (prendre sa retraite) ni « remove ». « Opt in » = accepter expressément ; « opt out » = refuser ou se désinscrire.

fr: dossier du personnel / dossier individuel du salarié
def: The set of records an employer keeps about an individual employee.

formal.ex: A copy of this letter will be placed on your [[personnel file]].

everyday.ex: There's nothing about a warning in her [[HR file]].
everyday.ex_us: There's nothing about a warning in her [[employee file]].

collocations: to place a document on file
to have access to one's personnel file
note_fr: « Personnel » (accent sur la dernière syllabe : /ˌpɜːsəˈnel/) ne se confond pas avec « personal » /ˈpɜːs(ə)n(ə)l/. Britanniques : « on your file » ; Américains : « in your file ». Plusieurs États américains donnent au salarié un droit d'accès à son dossier, sans règle fédérale générale.

def: To store a document or piece of information so that it can be consulted later.

formal.ex: Application documents are [[retained]] for no longer than is necessary for the recruitment process.

everyday.ex: We'd like to [[keep your CV on file]] in case something suitable comes up.
everyday.ex_us: We'd like to [[keep your résumé on file]] in case something suitable comes up.

informal.ex: Don't [[hang on to]] old interview notes just in case.

collocations: to keep a record of something
note_fr: « Conserver des données » = « to retain » ou « to keep », jamais « to conserve » (préserver, économiser). Le nom correspondant est « retention ». CV se dit « CV » au Royaume-Uni, « résumé » aux États-Unis.

def: The length of time for which a category of data may be kept before it must be deleted or anonymised.

formal.ex: The [[retention period]] applicable to each category of data is set out in the schedule below.

everyday.ex: The form should tell candidates what we collect and [[how long we keep it]].

collocations: to keep data for no longer than necessary
note_fr: Ne dites pas « conservation duration » ni « duration of conservation ». Le RGPD ne fixe pas de durées chiffrées : c'est à l'employeur de les déterminer et de les justifier, en s'aidant des recommandations de la CNIL (ou de l'ICO au Royaume-Uni).

def: To remove data permanently so that it can no longer be retrieved.

formal.ex: Data shall be securely [[erased]] upon expiry of the applicable retention period.

everyday.ex: Have the interview notes been [[deleted]] from the shared drive as well?

informal.ex: We really need to [[get rid of]] those old spreadsheets.

collocations: to delete data from a system
note_fr: « Supprimer » = « to delete » ; « to suppress » veut dire étouffer ou réprimer et serait un contresens. « Erase » et « erasure » appartiennent au vocabulaire du RGPD ; au quotidien, on dit « delete ».

def: A security incident in which personal data is lost, destroyed, altered, or disclosed to or accessed by someone who should not have it.

formal.ex: Any suspected [[personal data breach]] must be reported to the Data Protection Officer without delay.

everyday.ex: It's only one email, but strictly speaking it's still a [[breach]].

note_fr: « Violation » se dit « breach » /briːtʃ/ ; le mot anglais « violation » s'emploie pour une infraction à une règle (« a violation of the policy », surtout aux États-Unis). Une fiche de paie envoyée au mauvais destinataire est déjà un « data breach ».

def: To inform the person or authority responsible that a data breach has occurred.

formal.ex: The controller shall [[notify]] the supervisory authority of the breach without undue delay.

everyday.ex: If you send something to the wrong person, [[report]] it straight away. Nobody will blame you.
everyday.ex_us: If you send something to the wrong person, [[report]] it right away. Nobody will blame you.

note_fr: Construction : « to notify someone of something » (on notifie la personne), ou « to report something to someone ». Évitez « to notify a breach to the authority ». En droit de l'Union, la notification à l'autorité doit intervenir si possible dans les 72 heures.

fr: délégué à la protection des données (DPO)
def: The person appointed to advise an organisation on its data protection obligations and to monitor its compliance.

formal.ex: Requests should be addressed to the [[Data Protection Officer]], whose contact details appear below.

everyday.ex: I'd check with the [[DPO]] before we send anything out.

collocations: to refer a matter to the DPO
note_fr: En anglais, on garde le sigle DPO (jamais « DPD »). Le DPO conseille et contrôle, mais ne décide pas : la responsabilité reste celle de l'employeur. Il ne peut pas être sanctionné pour avoir exercé ses missions. Aux États-Unis, la fonction voisine est le « (chief) privacy officer », sans statut protecteur comparable.

def: The public body responsible for enforcing data protection law.

formal.ex: You have the right to lodge a complaint with the competent [[supervisory authority]].
formal.ex_us: You have the right to file a complaint with the competent [[regulatory authority]].

everyday.ex: If [[the regulator]] ever asks, we need to be able to show why we kept it.

collocations: to be investigated by the regulator
to be fined by the regulator
note_fr: « Supervisory authority » est le terme du RGPD ; à l'oral, tout le monde dit « the regulator ». En France, c'est la CNIL ; au Royaume-Uni, l'ICO. Aux États-Unis, il n'existe pas d'autorité unique : le rôle se partage entre la FTC, les procureurs généraux des États et quelques agences d'État.

term.uk: the CNIL (the French data protection authority)
term.us: the CNIL (the French data protection authority)

def: France's independent data protection regulator, which issues guidance, handles complaints, carries out inspections and can impose fines.

formal.ex: The system has been designed in line with the guidance published by [[the French data protection authority]] (CNIL).

everyday.ex: [[The French regulator]] takes a pretty firm line on tracking employees.

collocations: to be fined by the CNIL
note_fr: Le sigle ne dit rien à un interlocuteur étranger : glosez-le à la première occurrence, puis écrivez « the CNIL ». L'équivalent britannique est l'ICO (Information Commissioner's Office) ; il n'y a pas d'équivalent fédéral américain.

explain.written: The CNIL (Commission nationale de l'informatique et des libertés) is the independent French authority responsible for enforcing data protection law; it publishes guidance for employers, investigates complaints and may impose fines.
explain.spoken: The CNIL is the French data protection regulator - basically the French counterpart of the ICO in the UK.

def: A request by an individual to be told what personal data an organisation holds about them and to receive a copy of it.

formal.ex: The Company will respond to any [[data subject access request]] within the statutory time limit.

everyday.ex: We've had a [[DSAR]] from someone who left in the spring.
everyday.ex_us: We've had an [[access request]] from someone who left in the spring.

collocations: to make a subject access request
note_fr: Au Royaume-Uni, tout professionnel RH connaît le sigle DSAR (ou SAR), devenu une arme classique dans les litiges. Le droit porte sur les données, pas nécessairement sur les documents entiers. Aux États-Unis, un droit comparable n'existe que dans certains États, par exemple la Californie.

def: To make information known or available to someone else.

formal.ex: Personal data shall not be [[disclosed]] to any third party without lawful authority.

everyday.ex: Please don't [[pass on]] her home address to anyone outside the team.

informal.ex: Somebody [[let slip]] that he'd applied for another job.

collocations: to disclose information to a third party
note_fr: « Communiquer des données à quelqu'un » se dit « to disclose data to someone », pas « to communicate data ». « Divulguer » au sens fautif se rend par « unauthorised disclosure » ou « to leak ».

def: On the understanding that the information will not be passed on to anyone else.

formal.ex: All information provided in the course of the process will be treated [[in strict confidence]].

everyday.ex: Just [[between ourselves]], she's been off with stress.
everyday.ex_us: Just [[between us]], she's been out with stress.

informal.ex: I'd [[keep that to yourself]] for now.

collocations: to tell someone something in confidence
note_fr: Faux ami : « confidence » signifie d'abord « confiance en soi » ; l'adjectif « confidential » = confidentiel, « confident » = sûr de soi. « In confidence » = sous le sceau du secret.

fr: accès limité aux seules personnes habilitées
def: Sharing information only with the people who require it in order to do their job.

formal.ex: Access to medical information is granted [[strictly on a need-to-know basis]].

everyday.uk: only the people who need to know
everyday.us: only the people who need to know
everyday.ex: Let's keep this to [[only the people who need to know]].

note_fr: Expression très idiomatique, à préférer au calque « habilitated persons ». « Personnes habilitées » = « authorised staff » ou « those with a need to know ».

def: Any means by which an employer observes or records what employees do at work, such as checking emails or internet use.

formal.ex: The Company reserves the right to [[monitor]] the use of its IT systems for the purposes set out below.

everyday.ex: They want to [[keep an eye on]] how much time people spend on personal browsing.

informal.ex: Staff will think we're [[snooping on]] them.

note_fr: « Monitoring » est le mot neutre ; « surveillance » en anglais est plus fort et évoque la police ou l'espionnage. « To control employees » serait un faux ami : « to control » = diriger, maîtriser, pas contrôler au sens de vérifier (« to check », « to monitor »).

def: Cameras installed on premises to record what happens there, mainly for security purposes.

formal.ex: A [[CCTV system]] operates at the entrances to the building for the protection of persons and property.
formal.ex_us: A [[video surveillance system]] operates at the entrances to the building for the protection of persons and property.

everyday.ex: There are [[CCTV cameras]] in the car park, but none on the shop floor.
everyday.ex_us: There are [[security cameras]] in the parking lot, but none on the shop floor.

note_fr: « CCTV » (closed-circuit television) est le terme britannique courant ; les Américains disent « security cameras » ou « video surveillance ». Les images se disent « footage » (indénombrable). En France, filmer en continu un salarié à son poste est en principe jugé disproportionné.

def: An inquiry into a candidate's past, such as qualifications, previous employment or criminal record, carried out before hiring.

formal.ex: Any offer of employment is conditional upon satisfactory [[background screening]].

everyday.uk: to run a background check on
everyday.us: to run a background check on
everyday.ex: Do you [[run a background check on]] every new hire, or only on finance roles?

informal.ex: Everyone on that contract has to be [[vetted]].

collocations: to carry out a background check
note_fr: Pratique banale aux États-Unis, où elle est encadrée par une loi fédérale sur les rapports de solvabilité et d'antécédents (information et autorisation écrite du candidat). En France, l'employeur ne peut recueillir que des informations ayant un lien direct et nécessaire avec le poste : ne promettez pas à un client américain un « full background check ».

def: The information collected about people who apply for a job, such as CVs, interview notes and test results.

formal.ex: [[Candidate data]] is collected solely for the purpose of assessing suitability for the role applied for.
formal.ex_us: [[Applicant data]] is collected solely for the purpose of assessing suitability for the role applied for.

everyday.ex: Where do we keep [[candidates' details]] once a vacancy has closed?
everyday.ex_us: Where do we keep [[applicants' information]] once a position has closed?

note_fr: « Candidat » = « candidate » (plutôt UK) ou « applicant » (plutôt US, et pour celui qui vient de postuler). Attention aux notes d'entretien : elles sont communicables au candidat qui exerce son droit d'accès, d'où l'intérêt de n'y écrire que des appréciations objectives.

def: Correct, and reflecting the person's current situation.

formal.ex: Employees are responsible for ensuring that the information they provide remains [[accurate and up to date]].

everyday.ex: Could you remind everyone to [[update their details]] on the portal before payroll runs?
everyday.ex_us: Could you remind everyone to [[update their details]] in the portal before payroll runs?

collocations: to keep records up to date
to notify HR of any change
note_fr: « Exact » se dit « accurate » ; « exact » en anglais signifie « précis au chiffre près ». « Actualiser » = « to update », jamais « to actualise ». Trait d'union devant un nom : « up-to-date records ».

fr: données sensibles / catégories particulières de données
def: Types of personal data that receive extra protection, such as health, ethnic origin, religion, trade union membership, sexual orientation and biometric data.

formal.ex: [[Special categories of personal data]] are processed only where one of the conditions laid down by law is met.
formal.ex_us: [[Sensitive personal information]] is processed only where one of the conditions laid down by law is met.

everyday.ex: Anything about health counts as [[sensitive data]], so it stays with HR.
everyday.ex_us: Anything about health counts as [[sensitive information]], so it stays with HR.

collocations: data revealing racial or ethnic origin
note_fr: « Special category data » est l'expression britannique consacrée ; « sensitive data » passe partout à l'oral. Attention : le salaire ou les coordonnées bancaires sont confidentiels, mais ne sont pas des « special categories » au sens du RGPD. Les données sur les condamnations pénales relèvent d'un régime à part.

def: Information about a person's physical or mental health, including sickness records and medical reports.

formal.ex: [[Data concerning health]] is accessible only to the occupational health service.
formal.ex_us: [[Medical information]] is accessible only to designated personnel and is kept apart from the personnel file.

everyday.ex: A manager needs to know when someone's off, not their [[medical details]].
everyday.ex_us: A manager needs to know when someone's out, not their [[medical information]].

note_fr: En France, l'employeur n'a pas à connaître le diagnostic : l'arrêt de travail ne le mentionne pas et le médecin du travail ne lui transmet qu'un avis d'aptitude. Au Royaume-Uni, les questionnaires de santé sont plus répandus ; aux États-Unis, le droit fédéral impose de conserver les informations médicales dans un dossier séparé et confidentiel.

def: The permissions that determine which users can see or change particular data in a system.

formal.ex: [[Access permissions]] are reviewed whenever an employee changes role or leaves the Company.

everyday.ex: Why do line managers [[have access to]] the whole salary file?

note_fr: Ne confondez pas « access rights » (habilitations dans un système) et « the right of access » (droit d'accès de la personne à ses données). « Habilitation » ne se traduit pas par « habilitation » : dites « permissions » ou « authorisation ».

fr: conformité (en matière de protection des données)
def: The state of meeting the requirements of data protection law, and the work needed to get there.

formal.ex: The HR Director is responsible for ensuring [[compliance with]] this policy.

everyday.ex: Honestly, I'm not sure our recruitment process would [[be compliant]] if anyone looked closely.
everyday.ex_us: Honestly, I'm not sure our hiring process would [[be in compliance]] if anyone looked closely.

informal.ex: It [[ticks the boxes]], but nobody actually reads the notice.
informal.ex_us: It [[checks the boxes]], but nobody actually reads the notice.

collocations: to bring a process into line with the law
note_fr: « Conformité » = « compliance » (avec « with ») ; « conformity » existe mais ne s'emploie pas dans ce sens. « Mise en conformité » se rend par un verbe : « to bring something into compliance » ou « to become compliant ».

def: Any person or organisation other than the employer and the individual the data is about.

formal.ex: The Company will not transfer your data to any [[third party]] except as described in this notice.

everyday.ex: We never give references to [[anyone outside the company]] without checking with the employee first.

collocations: to share data with a third party
to pass data to a third party
note_fr: « Tiers » = « third party » (pluriel « third parties »), avec trait d'union en position d'adjectif : « a third-party provider ». Pas de « a third » ni de « a tier », qui désigne un niveau.

fr: droit au respect de la vie privée
def: The right of a person to keep their personal life and communications free from unjustified interference, including at work.

formal.uk: the right to respect for private life
formal.us: the right to respect for private life
formal.ex: Employees retain [[the right to respect for private life]] in the workplace and during working hours.

everyday.ex: People are entitled to some [[privacy]] at work, even on a company laptop.

note_fr: « Vie privée » = « private life » ou « privacy » selon le contexte ; « intimacy » désigne l'intimité affective ou physique et serait un contresens. En France et au Royaume-Uni, le salarié conserve une part de vie privée au travail ; aux États-Unis, l'employeur qui a prévenu par écrit dispose d'une marge bien plus large.

def: The information needed to reach someone: address, telephone number and email address.

formal.ex: Employees must notify the HR department promptly of any change to their [[contact details]].
formal.ex_us: Employees must notify the HR department promptly of any change to their [[contact information]].

everyday.ex: Can you check we've got the right [[details]] for her next of kin?
everyday.ex_us: Can you check we've got the right [[info]] for her emergency contact?

note_fr: Faux ami : « coordinates » ne désigne que des coordonnées géographiques. Coordonnées bancaires = « bank details » (UK) ou « bank account information » (US) ; le RIB n'existe pas à l'étranger. Personne à prévenir = « emergency contact » ou, au Royaume-Uni, « next of kin ».

def: The legal ground that allows an organisation to process personal data in a given case.

formal.ex: The [[lawful basis for processing]] your bank details is the performance of your employment contract.
formal.ex_us: The [[legal basis for processing]] your bank account information is the performance of your employment contract.

everyday.ex: Before we start collecting it, we need to be clear about [[what we're relying on]].

collocations: to rely on a lawful basis
to have no lawful basis for something
note_fr: Le verbe à retenir est « to rely on » : « we rely on legitimate interests ». Pluriel irrégulier : one basis /ˈbeɪsɪs/, two bases /ˈbeɪsiːz/. Le RGPD prévoit six bases ; en matière RH, les plus courantes sont le contrat, l'obligation légale et l'intérêt légitime.

def: A lawful basis allowing data to be processed for a genuine business reason, provided this is not outweighed by the rights of the individuals concerned.

formal.ex: The processing is necessary for the purposes of the [[legitimate interests]] pursued by the Company, namely the security of its premises.

everyday.ex: You need [[a good business reason]], and it has to outweigh the intrusion.

note_fr: Presque toujours au pluriel dans l'usage britannique. Ce n'est pas un blanc-seing : il faut mettre en balance (« balancing test ») l'intérêt de l'employeur et les droits des salariés, et en garder une trace écrite.

term.uk: necessary for the performance of the contract
term.us: necessary for the performance of the contract

ipa.uk: /ˌnesəs(ə)ri fə ðə pəˈfɔːməns əv ðə ˈkɒntrækt/
ipa.us: /ˌnesəseri fər ðə pərˈfɔːrməns əv ðə ˈkɑːntrækt/

def: Required in order to carry out the employment contract, for example using bank details to pay a salary.

formal.uk: necessary for the performance of the contract
formal.us: necessary for the performance of the contract
formal.ex: The processing of payroll data is [[necessary for the performance of the contract]] of employment.

everyday.uk: we can't employ someone without it
everyday.us: we can't employ someone without it
everyday.ex: Bank details are easy: [[we can't employ someone without them]].

collocations: necessary for compliance with a legal obligation
note_fr: « Exécution du contrat » = « performance of the contract » ; « execution » d'un contrat signifie sa signature, source classique de contresens. « Necessary » est interprété strictement : utile ou pratique ne suffit pas.

def: The specific reason for which personal data is collected and used.

formal.uk: for specified, explicit and legitimate purposes
formal.us: for specified, explicit and legitimate purposes
formal.ex: Personal data shall be collected [[for specified, explicit and legitimate purposes]] and not further processed in a manner incompatible with them.

everyday.ex: If we can't say [[what it's for]], we shouldn't be asking for it.

collocations: to use data for a different purpose
note_fr: « Finalité » se dit « purpose » /ˈpɜːpəs/ (deuxième syllabe très réduite), jamais « finality », qui signifie « caractère définitif ». Le détournement de finalité se décrit par « using data for a purpose other than the one it was collected for ».

def: The principle that an organisation should collect and keep only the data it actually needs for its purpose.

formal.uk: adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary
formal.us: adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary
formal.ex: The information requested from candidates shall be [[adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary]].

everyday.ex: Let's collect [[only what we actually need]]. Why are we asking for marital status at the application stage?

collocations: nice to have rather than necessary
note_fr: Orthographe : -isation au Royaume-Uni, -ization aux États-Unis. À l'oral, mieux vaut la formule simple « only what we need » que le terme technique. Exemples classiques de collecte excessive : situation de famille, numéro de sécurité sociale ou photo dès la candidature.

def: Going no further than is needed to achieve a legitimate aim.

formal.ex: Any monitoring must be justified by the nature of the task and [[proportionate to the aim pursued]].

everyday.ex: Tracking every van around the clock feels a bit [[over the top]] to me.
everyday.ex_us: Tracking every van around the clock feels like [[overkill]] to me.

informal.ex: Reading everyone's messages because of one leak would be pretty [[heavy-handed]].

note_fr: Dites « proportionate » (et « disproportionate ») plutôt que « proportional », réservé aux rapports mathématiques. La formule française « justifié par la nature de la tâche et proportionné au but recherché » se rend très bien mot pour mot.

def: The written inventory an organisation must keep of the ways in which it uses personal data.

formal.ex: The recruitment platform has been entered in the Company's [[record of processing activities]].

everyday.ex: Is the new appraisal tool in the [[processing register]] yet?
everyday.ex_us: Is the new appraisal tool in the [[data inventory]] yet?

collocations: to maintain a record of processing
to add an entry to the record
to keep the record up to date
note_fr: Le nom « record » s'accentue sur la première syllabe (/ˈrekɔːd/), le verbe sur la seconde (/rɪˈkɔːd/). Le sigle ROPA est courant chez les spécialistes britanniques. La dispense prévue pour les entreprises de moins de 250 salariés ne joue pas pour les traitements réguliers : la gestion du personnel doit donc y figurer.

def: The right of an individual to have inaccurate data about them corrected and incomplete data completed.

formal.ex: You are entitled [[to have inaccurate data rectified]] without undue delay.

everyday.ex: He wants to [[get his appraisal record corrected]]. The rating on the system isn't the one he was given.

collocations: to add a note to the file
note_fr: « Rectify » est juridique ; au quotidien, on dit « correct ». Ce droit vise les faits inexacts, non les appréciations : un salarié ne peut pas faire « rectifier » une évaluation qu'il conteste, mais peut demander que son désaccord soit consigné.

def: The right of an individual to have their data deleted in certain circumstances, for example when it is no longer needed.

formal.ex: [[The right to erasure]] does not apply where the Company is required by law to retain the data.

everyday.ex: He's quoting [[the right to be forgotten]], but we have to keep payroll records anyway.

collocations: to ask for one's data to be deleted
note_fr: Ce droit n'est pas absolu : l'employeur peut refuser lorsqu'une obligation légale de conservation s'applique ou que les données sont nécessaires à sa défense en justice. « Erasure » : /ɪˈreɪʒə/ au Royaume-Uni, /ɪˈreɪʃər/ aux États-Unis.

def: The right of an individual to ask an organisation to stop processing their data on grounds relating to their particular situation.

formal.ex: You have the right [[to object to the processing]] of your data on grounds relating to your particular situation.

everyday.ex: Does anyone [[have an objection to]] being in the team photo?

note_fr: Le verbe s'accentue sur la seconde syllabe (/əbˈdʒekt/), le nom « an object » sur la première. Construction : « to object to + nom ou -ing » (« he objected to being filmed »), jamais « object against ».

def: To hide or remove parts of a document, typically names or confidential passages, before disclosing it.

formal.ex: Information identifying other individuals has been [[redacted]] from the enclosed documents.

everyday.ex: We'll have to [[black out]] the witnesses' names before it goes to him.

note_fr: Faux ami total : « to redact » ne veut pas dire « rédiger » (to draft, to write) mais « occulter ». « Redaction » = occultation. Indispensable pour répondre à une demande d'accès sans porter atteinte aux droits des tiers.

def: The period within which an organisation must answer a request made by an individual about their data.

formal.ex: The Company shall respond to your request [[within one month of receipt]].

everyday.ex: The request came in on the 3rd, so [[the clock is ticking]].

note_fr: « Délai » = « time limit », « deadline » ou « period » ; « delay » signifie « retard ». Au titre du RGPD, le délai est d'un mois, prolongeable de deux mois pour les demandes complexes, à condition d'en informer le demandeur. « Within » = dans un délai de ; « in one month » = dans un mois.

def: The document setting out how employees may use the employer's IT systems and how that use may be monitored.

formal.ex: Use of the Company's systems is governed by the [[IT acceptable use policy]], a copy of which is appended to the internal rules.

everyday.ex: It's in the [[IT policy]]: reasonable personal use is fine, streaming all afternoon isn't.

collocations: to sign up to the policy
to be in breach of the IT policy
to append the policy to the internal rules
note_fr: « Charter » évoque un texte solennel (charte royale, charte des Nations unies) : pour un document interne, dites « policy ». Particularité française à expliquer : la charte n'est opposable disciplinairement que si elle a suivi la procédure du règlement intérieur, notamment la consultation du CSE.

explain.written: The charte informatique is the French employer's IT acceptable use policy; to be enforceable through disciplinary action, it is generally adopted under the same procedure as the company's internal rules, including consultation of the works council.
explain.spoken: It's our IT acceptable use policy - and in France, if you want to be able to discipline people for breaking it, it has to go through the works council first.

def: Use of the employer's equipment, email or internet access for private rather than work purposes.

formal.ex: [[Reasonable personal use]] of the Company's internet access is permitted, provided that it does not interfere with the employee's duties.

everyday.ex: Nobody minds if you use the laptop [[for your own stuff]] at lunchtime.

note_fr: Le nom « use » se prononce /juːs/, le verbe « to use » /juːz/. En France, un usage personnel raisonnable des outils professionnels est toléré et ne peut pas être totalement interdit ; aux États-Unis, la politique interne peut être beaucoup plus restrictive.

def: The use of a device to record where a company vehicle or an employee is at a given time.

formal.ex: The [[geolocation system]] fitted to company vehicles shall not be used to monitor compliance with speed limits.

everyday.ex: All the vans have a [[tracker]], but drivers can switch it off outside working hours.
everyday.ex_us: All the vans have a [[GPS tracker]], but drivers can turn it off outside working hours.

note_fr: « Geolocation » existe mais reste technique ; à l'oral, « tracking ». En France, la géolocalisation ne peut pas servir à contrôler le temps de travail lorsqu'un autre moyen existe, ni à suivre des salariés libres d'organiser leurs déplacements, et elle doit pouvoir être désactivée hors temps de travail.

def: A card that employees use to enter premises, and which records the time and place of each entry.

formal.ex: Data generated by the [[access control system]] is retained for three months.

everyday.ex: The door logs show he [[swiped in]] at ten past nine.
everyday.ex_us: The door logs show he [[badged in]] at ten after nine.

note_fr: « Badge » en anglais désigne plutôt un insigne ou un porte-nom ; la carte d'accès est « swipe card », « access card », « pass » (UK) ou « key card » (US). « Badgeuse » = « time clock » ; pointer = « to clock in / clock out ».

def: An arrangement under which employees use their own phone, tablet or computer for work.

formal.ex: Employees who use [[personally owned devices]] for work purposes must comply with the security requirements set out below.

everyday.ex: Half the sales team read their work email on [[their own phones]].

informal.ex: We've never had a proper [[BYOD]] policy.

collocations: to keep work and personal data separate
note_fr: Le sigle BYOD s'épelle lettre par lettre. Point de vigilance : l'employeur reste responsable des données professionnelles stockées sur l'appareil, mais ne peut pas accéder au contenu privé du salarié.

def: To introduce a new system or tool gradually across an organisation.

formal.ex: No monitoring system shall be [[introduced]] before employees have been informed and their representatives consulted.

everyday.ex: They're planning to [[roll out]] the new time-tracking app in January.

collocations: to roll out a tool across the group
to put a system in place
note_fr: « To deploy » s'emploie aussi, mais « roll out » est le verbe naturel en entreprise ; nom : « a roll-out » (UK) ou « a rollout » (US). En France, tout dispositif de contrôle de l'activité suppose l'information préalable des salariés et la consultation du CSE : faute de quoi la preuve recueillie est fragile.

fr: analyse d'impact relative à la protection des données (AIPD)
def: A documented analysis of the risks a planned use of data poses to individuals, and of the measures that will reduce them.

formal.ex: A [[data protection impact assessment]] shall be carried out before any processing likely to result in a high risk to individuals.

everyday.ex: Has anyone done a [[DPIA]] on the new monitoring tool?
everyday.ex_us: Has anyone done an [[impact assessment]] on the new monitoring tool?

collocations: likely to result in a high risk
note_fr: En anglais, le sigle est DPIA (et non AIPD). On dit « to carry out » ou « to conduct » une analyse, pas « to make ». La CNIL a publié une liste de traitements pour lesquels elle est obligatoire, dont la surveillance constante de l'activité des salariés et les dispositifs d'alerte professionnelle.

def: The contract between a controller and a processor that sets out what the processor may do with the data and how it must protect it.

formal.ex: The Supplier shall enter into a [[data processing agreement]] in the form set out in Schedule 3.

everyday.ex: Did the payroll people ever sign a [[DPA]]?

note_fr: Attention à l'ambiguïté du sigle : au Royaume-Uni, « the DPA » désigne aussi la loi nationale sur la protection des données (Data Protection Act), et parfois une « data protection authority ». Le contexte tranche.

def: The software an organisation uses to store and manage its employee records, payroll, absences and appraisals.

formal.ex: Employee records are held in the Company's [[human resources information system]], which is hosted within the European Union.

everyday.ex: Everything's on the [[HR system]] now, so we've stopped keeping paper files.
everyday.ex_us: Everything's in the [[HR system]] now, so we've stopped keeping paper files.

collocations: to log in to the HR system
to migrate data to a new system
note_fr: Le sigle anglais est HRIS, prononcé lettre par lettre ou « H-ris » ; « SIRH » est inconnu hors de France. On dit aussi « HR platform » ou « HR software ».

def: Altering data irreversibly so that no individual can be identified from it any longer.

formal.ex: Survey responses are [[anonymised]] before being shared with management.
formal.ex_us: Survey responses are [[anonymized]] before being shared with management.

everyday.ex: Can you [[strip out the names]] before you send the figures to the board?

collocations: to report on an anonymous basis
note_fr: Attention aux petits effectifs : une statistique « anonyme » portant sur une équipe de trois personnes ne l'est pas. Si la réidentification reste possible, il s'agit de pseudonymisation et le RGPD continue de s'appliquer.

def: Converting data into a coded form that can only be read by someone who has the key.

formal.ex: Personal data stored on portable devices shall be [[encrypted]].

everyday.ex: Is the spreadsheet at least [[password-protected]]?

note_fr: Le verbe est « to encrypt » ; « to crypt » n'existe pas. Un ordinateur portable perdu mais chiffré présente un risque bien moindre pour les personnes, ce qui pèse sur l'obligation de notifier la violation.

def: To take immediate steps to stop a data breach from spreading or causing further harm.

formal.ex: Immediate steps were taken to [[contain]] the incident and to recover the data.

everyday.ex: Have we tried to [[recall]] the email, or asked them to delete it?

collocations: to ask the recipient to delete it
note_fr: « To recall an email » = rappeler un message envoyé par erreur. « Contain » se dit d'un incident, d'un risque, d'une fuite ; ne traduisez pas « maîtriser » par « to master ».

def: Describes an email or document delivered by mistake to someone other than the person intended.

formal.ex: A file containing salary information was [[sent in error]] to an external recipient.

everyday.uk: to go to the wrong person
everyday.us: to go to the wrong person
everyday.ex: The payslips [[went to the wrong person]] because of autocomplete.
everyday.ex_us: The pay stubs [[went to the wrong person]] because of autocomplete.

collocations: to copy someone in by mistake
note_fr: « Par erreur » = « in error » (soutenu) ou « by mistake » (courant), pas « by error ». Mettre en copie = « to copy someone in » (UK), « to cc someone » (US et UK). L'erreur de destinataire est la cause la plus banale de violation de données RH.

def: The set of documents gathered during an internal investigation, such as complaints, interview notes and the final report.

formal.ex: Access to the [[investigation file]] is restricted to the investigators and the HR Director.

everyday.ex: Keep the [[investigation papers]] out of the general HR folder.
everyday.ex_us: Keep the [[investigation papers]] out of the general HR folder.

collocations: to keep the file under restricted access
note_fr: Un dossier d'enquête contient des données sur le plaignant, la personne mise en cause et les témoins : chacun conserve ses droits, mais l'accès de l'un ne doit pas porter atteinte aux droits des autres. Pensez à fixer une durée de conservation dès l'ouverture.

def: A person who applied for a job but was not offered it.

formal.ex: Data relating to [[unsuccessful candidates]] is deleted at the end of the retention period notified to them.
formal.ex_us: Data relating to [[unsuccessful applicants]] is deleted at the end of the retention period notified to them.

everyday.uk: the ones who didn't get the job
everyday.us: the ones who didn't get the job
everyday.ex: What do we do with the CVs of [[the ones who didn't get the job]]?
everyday.ex_us: What do we do with the résumés of [[the ones who didn't get the job]]?

collocations: to keep a CV on file
note_fr: Jamais « a refused candidate » ni « a non-retained candidate ». La CNIL recommande de ne pas conserver les dossiers au-delà de deux ans après le dernier contact, et d'informer le candidat qu'il peut s'y opposer ; l'ICO britannique laisse l'employeur fixer et justifier sa propre durée.

def: A database of people who might be suitable for future vacancies.

formal.ex: With your agreement, your application will be retained in our [[talent pool]] for a period of two years.

everyday.ex: She wasn't right for this role, but I'd like to [[keep her in mind]] for the next one.

collocations: to add someone to the talent pool
to be considered for other roles
note_fr: « Vivier » ne se traduit pas littéralement : « talent pool » ou « candidate pool ». C'est l'un des rares cas, en matière RH, où demander l'accord de la personne a un sens, puisqu'elle peut refuser sans conséquence.

fr: consultation des réseaux sociaux des candidats
def: Looking at a candidate's social media profiles as part of the recruitment process.

formal.ex: Recruiters may [[consult publicly available profiles]] of a professional nature only.

everyday.ex: Let's be honest, every hiring manager [[looks candidates up online]].

informal.ex: Did you [[google]] him before the interview?

note_fr: Dites « social media » plutôt que « social networks ». En France, les informations recueillies sur un candidat doivent avoir un lien direct et nécessaire avec l'emploi proposé, ce qui exclut en principe les comptes personnels. Aux États-Unis, plusieurs États interdisent d'exiger les mots de passe des candidats.

def: The official number that identifies a person for tax and social security purposes.

formal.ex: Your [[National Insurance number]] is used solely for payroll and statutory reporting purposes.
formal.ex_us: Your [[Social Security number]] is used solely for payroll and statutory reporting purposes.

everyday.ex: We don't need their [[NI number]] until they've actually accepted the offer.
everyday.ex_us: We don't need their [[Social]] until they've actually accepted the offer.

note_fr: Pas d'équivalent unique : « National Insurance number » au Royaume-Uni, « Social Security number » (SSN) aux États-Unis ; pour le numéro français, dites « French social security number ». Son usage est strictement encadré en France (paie et déclarations sociales) ; aux États-Unis, c'est la donnée la plus exposée à l'usurpation d'identité.

def: An inquiry into whether a person has criminal convictions, carried out for certain jobs.

formal.ex: Appointment to this post is subject to a satisfactory [[criminal record check]].
formal.ex_us: Appointment to this position is subject to a satisfactory [[criminal background check]].

everyday.ex: Anyone working with children needs a [[DBS check]].
everyday.ex_us: Anyone working with children needs a [[criminal check]].

collocations: an extract from the criminal record
note_fr: Au Royaume-Uni, la vérification passe par un organisme public (« DBS check ») et dépend du type de poste. En France, l'employeur ne peut demander un extrait de casier (bulletin n° 3) que si le poste le justifie, et ne doit pas en conserver de copie. Aux États-Unis, de nombreux États et villes interdisent de poser la question avant un certain stade du recrutement (lois « ban-the-box »).

term.uk: to remove a warning from the file
term.us: to remove a warning from the file

ipa.uk: /tə rɪˌmuːv ə ˈwɔːnɪŋ frəm ðə ˈfaɪl/
ipa.us: /tə rɪˌmuːv ə ˈwɔːrnɪŋ frəm ðə ˈfaɪl/

def: To take a disciplinary warning out of an employee's records once it is no longer valid.

formal.uk: to be disregarded for disciplinary purposes
formal.us: to be disregarded for disciplinary purposes
formal.ex: The warning shall [[be disregarded for disciplinary purposes]] after twelve months.

everyday.ex: The warning should have [[come off the file]] ages ago.

informal.ex: After a year, it's supposed to [[wipe the slate clean]].

note_fr: Au Royaume-Uni, un avertissement « expire » après la durée fixée par la procédure interne (on parle de « live » et de « spent warning »). En France, aucune sanction antérieure de plus de trois ans ne peut être invoquée à l'appui d'une nouvelle sanction : pensez-y en fixant les durées de conservation.

fr: l'ICO (autorité britannique de protection des données)
def: The United Kingdom's independent data protection regulator.

formal.ex: You may also raise your concern with [[the Information Commissioner's Office]].

everyday.ex: [[The ICO]] has detailed guidance on monitoring workers, so I'd start there.

collocations: to report a breach to the ICO
note_fr: Sigle épelé : I-C-O. C'est l'homologue de la CNIL, réputé plus pragmatique et moins porté sur les amendes à l'égard des employeurs. Ses guides pratiques, rédigés en anglais clair, sont une excellente source de vocabulaire.

term.uk: to lodge a complaint with the regulator
term.us: to file a complaint with the regulator

ipa.uk: /tə ˌlɒdʒ ə kəmˈpleɪnt wɪð ðə ˈreɡjuleɪtə/
ipa.us: /tə ˌfaɪl ə kəmˈpleɪnt wɪð ðə ˈreɡjəleɪtər/

def: To ask the data protection authority formally to look into the way an organisation has handled one's data.

formal.ex: If you are dissatisfied with our response, you are entitled to [[lodge a complaint with]] the supervisory authority.
formal.ex_us: If you are dissatisfied with our response, you are entitled to [[file a complaint with]] the regulatory authority.

everyday.ex: If we miss the deadline, he'll [[go to the regulator]], and frankly he'd have a point.

collocations: a complaint about a late response
note_fr: « Déposer une plainte » = « to lodge » (UK) ou « to file » (US) « a complaint with » ; pas « to deposit » ni « to put a complaint ». « Complaint » est le nom, « to complain » le verbe.

def: An examination by the regulator of how an organisation handles personal data, which may take place on its premises.

formal.ex: The authority may carry out [[an on-site inspection]] without prior notice.

everyday.ex: What would we show them if the regulator [[turned up]] tomorrow?
everyday.ex_us: What would we show them if the regulator [[showed up]] tomorrow?

note_fr: « Contrôle » de la CNIL = « inspection », « audit » ou « investigation » ; « a control » désigne une mesure de maîtrise des risques (« security controls »). Encore le faux ami contrôler / to control.

def: A sum of money that an organisation is ordered to pay as a penalty for breaking the law.

formal.ex: Infringements may give rise to an [[administrative fine]] of up to four per cent of worldwide annual turnover.
formal.ex_us: Violations may give rise to a [[civil penalty]] assessed for each violation.

everyday.ex: A retailer [[was fined]] for filming staff on the shop floor all day long.

informal.uk: to get hit with a fine
informal.us: to get hit with a fine
informal.ex: Nobody wants to [[get hit with a fine]] over a spreadsheet.

note_fr: On dit « to impose a fine on » ou « to fine a company » ; « amende » ne se dit ni « amend » (modifier) ni « penalty fee ». Le RGPD plafonne les amendes les plus lourdes à 20 millions d'euros ou 4 % du chiffre d'affaires annuel mondial ; aux États-Unis, les sanctions se calculent en général par infraction.

def: Training designed to make employees understand the rules on handling personal data and the risks of getting it wrong.

formal.ex: All staff with access to personal data shall [[receive training]] on their obligations at least once a year.

everyday.ex: Managers could do with [[a refresher]] on what they can and can't keep in their own files.

note_fr: « Sensibiliser » ne se traduit pas par « to sensibilise » : dites « to raise awareness of » ou « to train staff on ». « Training » est indénombrable : « a training » se dit « a training session » ou « a course ».

fr: messagerie d'un salarié ayant quitté l'entreprise
def: The work email account of someone who no longer works for the organisation.

formal.ex: The Company will [[deactivate the account]] on the employee's last day, after allowing him or her to retrieve any private messages.

everyday.ex: His mailbox should have been [[shut down]] the day he left, not three months later.

collocations: to forward emails to a colleague
note_fr: « A leaver » (UK) = un salarié sortant ; les Américains disent « a departing employee ». La CNIL recommande de fermer la boîte au départ du salarié, après l'avoir prévenu pour qu'il puisse récupérer ses messages privés ; la laisser ouverte et la lire pendant des mois est un grief classique.

def: To tell employees about a monitoring system, and what it will be used for, before it is switched on.

formal.ex: No information may be collected by means of a system of which employees have not been given [[prior notice]].
formal.ex_us: No information may be collected by means of a system of which employees have not been given [[prior written notice]].

everyday.ex: As long as we [[tell people upfront]] what we're logging and why, most of them accept it.

collocations: to acknowledge receipt of the policy
note_fr: « Préalable » = « prior » ou « in advance », pas « previous ». En droit français, un dispositif non porté à la connaissance des salariés ne peut en principe pas servir de preuve contre eux. Quelques États américains (New York, par exemple) imposent désormais un avis écrit de surveillance électronique.

fr: transfert de données hors de l'Union européenne
def: Sending personal data to, or making it accessible from, a country outside the European Economic Area.

formal.uk: to transfer data outside the European Economic Area
formal.us: to transfer data outside the European Economic Area
formal.ex: The Company will not [[transfer data outside the European Economic Area]] unless appropriate safeguards are in place.

everyday.uk: to send data to head office
everyday.us: to send data to head office
everyday.ex: Every time we [[send data to head office]] in Chicago, that's a transfer.

collocations: a transfer to a third country
note_fr: Un simple accès à distance depuis les États-Unis au SIRH hébergé en Europe constitue déjà un transfert : c'est le point que les sociétés mères américaines découvrent le plus souvent. Le nom « transfer » s'accentue sur la première syllabe, le verbe plutôt sur la seconde.

def: A system that identifies people by a physical characteristic, such as a fingerprint or face, before letting them into premises or systems.

formal.ex: [[Biometric data]] shall be processed only where access to the area concerned requires a particularly high level of security.

everyday.ex: They want a [[fingerprint scanner]] on the server room door, which is one thing. Using it for clocking in is quite another.

note_fr: Les données biométriques sont des données sensibles. La CNIL exclut la pointeuse à empreinte digitale pour le contrôle des horaires et exige, pour le contrôle d'accès, une justification précise et documentée. Aux États-Unis, l'Illinois impose un consentement écrit et ouvre un droit d'action aux salariés.

def: Monitoring carried out without the knowledge of the people being observed.

formal.ex: [[Covert monitoring]] will be authorised only in exceptional circumstances, where there are grounds to suspect serious wrongdoing.

everyday.ex: You can't just put a camera in the stockroom [[behind people's backs]].

informal.ex: It'll look as if we're [[spying on]] our own staff.

note_fr: « Covert » : /ˈkʌvət/ au Royaume-Uni, /ˈkoʊvɜːrt/ aux États-Unis ; contraire : « overt ». En France, la preuve issue d'un dispositif clandestin est en principe illicite ; le juge peut néanmoins l'admettre si elle est indispensable à l'exercice du droit à la preuve et que l'atteinte est proportionnée. Au Royaume-Uni, l'ICO l'admet à titre exceptionnel et pour une durée limitée.

def: Software that records everything a user types on a keyboard.

formal.ex: The installation of [[keystroke logging software]] on employees' workstations is prohibited save in exceptional circumstances relating to security.

everyday.ex: A [[keylogger]] on every laptop? No regulator in Europe would wear that.
everyday.ex_us: A [[keylogger]] on every laptop? No regulator in Europe would go for that.

note_fr: La CNIL juge ces outils disproportionnés, sauf impératif fort de sécurité. Le sujet est revenu avec le télétravail (« bossware » en anglais familier). « Not wear something » est un idiome britannique familier : ne pas accepter.

def: Deleting the data on a phone or laptop from a distance, typically when the device is lost or its user leaves.

formal.ex: The Company reserves the right to [[erase remotely]] any Company data held on a personally owned device.

everyday.ex: If someone loses their phone, IT can [[wipe]] the work profile without touching their photos.

note_fr: « To wipe » = effacer entièrement ; nom : « a remote wipe ». Dans une politique BYOD, précisez que seul l'espace professionnel peut être effacé : supprimer les photos personnelles d'un salarié serait une atteinte difficile à justifier.

fr: messages et fichiers identifiés comme personnels
def: Messages or files on a work computer that the employee has clearly labelled as private.

formal.ex: Files and messages [[identified as personal]] by the employee shall not be opened in his or her absence.

everyday.ex: Anything [[marked 'personal']] is off limits unless he's there when you open it.

collocations: to open a file in the employee's presence
note_fr: Règle jurisprudentielle française sans équivalent exact : tout ce qui se trouve sur l'outil professionnel est présumé professionnel et consultable par l'employeur, sauf ce que le salarié a identifié comme personnel, qui ne peut être ouvert qu'en sa présence ou après l'avoir dûment appelé. Aux États-Unis, une politique écrite suffit en général à écarter toute attente de confidentialité.

explain.written: Under French case law, files and emails on a work computer are presumed to be professional and may be consulted by the employer, except those the employee has identified as personal, which may in principle be opened only in the employee's presence or after he or she has been duly invited to attend.
explain.spoken: In France, anything on a work computer is assumed to be work-related, but if the employee has labelled a file or an email 'personal', you generally can't open it unless they're there.

def: Model contract terms approved by the European Commission that allow personal data to be sent lawfully to a country outside Europe.

formal.ex: Transfers to the parent company are governed by the [[standard contractual clauses]] adopted by the European Commission.

everyday.ex: Have the [[SCCs]] been signed between the French entity and the US parent?

note_fr: Sigle courant : SCCs. Le Royaume-Uni utilise ses propres instruments, en particulier un avenant britannique aux clauses européennes. Ne pas confondre avec un simple « standard contract ».

def: A formal finding by the European Commission that a country outside the EU protects personal data to an adequate standard, so that data can flow there freely.

formal.ex: The United Kingdom benefits from an [[adequacy decision]], with the result that no additional safeguards are required.

everyday.ex: The UK [[is treated as safe]], so sending the files to London isn't a problem.

collocations: to be covered by an adequacy decision
to be certified under the Data Privacy Framework
in the absence of an adequacy decision
note_fr: « Adequate » /ˈædɪkwət/ signifie « suffisant », pas « adéquat » au sens de « parfaitement adapté ». Pour les États-Unis, l'adéquation ne vaut que pour les entreprises certifiées au titre du cadre transatlantique en vigueur ; vérifiez toujours que le destinataire l'est bien, et pour les données RH.

def: A company engaged by a processor to carry out part of the processing on the controller's data.

formal.ex: The Supplier shall not engage any [[sub-processor]] without the prior written authorisation of the Customer.
formal.ex_us: The Supplier shall not engage any [[sub-processor]] without the prior written authorization of the Customer.

everyday.ex: The HR platform is fine, but do we know who [[their own suppliers]] are and where they host the data?
everyday.ex_us: The HR platform is fine, but do we know who [[their own vendors]] are and where they host the data?

collocations: to object to a new sub-processor
note_fr: Encore le faux ami : pas « sub-subcontractor ». Le sous-traitant reste pleinement responsable, à l'égard de l'employeur, de ce que font ses propres sous-traitants.

def: Replacing names with a code so that individuals cannot be identified without additional information that is kept separately.

formal.ex: [[Pseudonymised data]] remains personal data and is subject to this policy.
formal.ex_us: [[Pseudonymized data]] remains personal data and is subject to this policy.

everyday.ex: We [[replace names with codes]], and only HR holds the key.

note_fr: Le « p » initial est muet : /ˌsjuː-/ ou /ˌsuː-/. À la différence de l'anonymisation, la pseudonymisation est réversible : les données restent personnelles. Aux États-Unis, on parle volontiers de « de-identified data », notion voisine mais définie différemment selon les textes.

def: The practical steps an organisation takes to keep personal data secure, from encryption to staff training and access rules.

formal.ex: The Supplier shall implement [[appropriate technical and organisational measures]] to protect the data against unauthorised access.
formal.ex_us: The Supplier shall implement [[appropriate technical and organizational measures]] to protect the data against unauthorized access.

everyday.ex: Before we go live, the salary data needs to be properly [[locked down]].

note_fr: Formule figée des contrats, souvent abrégée en TOMs. « Mettre en œuvre » = « to implement » ou « to put in place ». Les lois américaines parlent plutôt de « reasonable security ».

def: The internal record in which an organisation documents every data breach, whether or not it was reported to the regulator.

formal.ex: The controller shall [[document]] every personal data breach, including its effects and the remedial action taken.

everyday.ex: Even if we decide not to report it, we still have to [[log]] it and note why.

collocations: to keep a record of the decision
note_fr: Toute violation doit être consignée en interne, même si elle n'est pas notifiée à l'autorité : c'est ce registre que le contrôleur demandera en premier. « To log » = consigner ; « log » = journal.

fr: confidentialité de l'identité de l'auteur du signalement
def: The duty to ensure that the name of a person who reports wrongdoing is not revealed to those who do not need to know it.

formal.uk: the identity of the reporting person
formal.us: the identity of the reporting person
formal.ex: [[The identity of the reporting person]] shall not be disclosed without his or her express consent, save to the judicial authorities.

everyday.ex: He's bound to ask [[who raised it]], and we simply can't tell him.

informal.ex: It took some courage to [[blow the whistle]] on her own manager.

note_fr: Le terme de la directive européenne est « reporting person » ; au quotidien, « whistleblower ». En France, la confidentialité couvre l'identité de l'auteur du signalement, celle des personnes visées et les informations recueillies ; la personne mise en cause ne peut donc pas obtenir le nom de l'auteur par le biais de son droit d'accès. « To raise a concern » est l'expression britannique consacrée pour « faire un signalement ».

def: Information about other people that is contained in a document also relating to the person who is asking to see it.

formal.ex: Where a document contains [[information relating to another individual]], the Company will consider whether it is reasonable to disclose it.

everyday.ex: Half those emails are full of [[other people's data]], so we can't just print the lot.

collocations: to protect the rights of others
to seek the other person's consent
note_fr: Notion centrale pour répondre à une demande d'accès : le droit d'accès ne doit pas porter atteinte aux droits et libertés d'autrui. D'où l'occultation (« redaction ») des noms des témoins ou des collègues, plutôt qu'un refus global.

def: To decide not to hand over information that has been requested.

formal.ex: Certain documents have been [[withheld]] on the ground that their disclosure would reveal the identity of a third party.

everyday.ex: We're entitled to [[hold back]] the legal advice, but not much else.

collocations: to withhold a document in full
note_fr: Verbe irrégulier : withhold, withheld, withheld ; un seul « h » prononcé. Toute rétention doit être motivée dans la réponse. Rien à voir ici avec « withholding tax » (retenue à la source), autre emploi du même verbe.

def: A rule that releases an organisation from an obligation in defined circumstances, for example allowing it not to disclose certain information.

formal.ex: Confidential references given by the Company [[fall within an exemption]] under United Kingdom law.

everyday.uk: to be covered by an exemption
everyday.us: to be covered by an exemption
everyday.ex: Management forecasts and negotiating positions [[are covered by an exemption]], at least in the UK.

note_fr: « Exemption » (dispense d'une obligation) se distingue d'« exception ». Le droit britannique énumère des exemptions détaillées (références confidentielles, prévisions de gestion, négociations en cours) que le droit français ne formule pas ainsi : n'exportez pas l'une chez l'autre sans vérifier.

def: The rule protecting confidential communications between a lawyer and a client from having to be disclosed.

formal.uk: to be subject to legal professional privilege
formal.us: to be protected by attorney-client privilege
formal.ex: Advice received from the Company's solicitors [[is subject to legal professional privilege]] and has not been disclosed.
formal.ex_us: Advice received from the Company's attorneys [[is protected by attorney-client privilege]] and has not been disclosed.

everyday.ex: Anything from our lawyers is [[privileged]], so it stays out of the bundle.
everyday.ex_us: Anything from our lawyers is [[privileged]], so it stays out of the production.

note_fr: Faux ami : « privilege » n'est pas ici un avantage mais une protection contre la divulgation. Différence de fond : au Royaume-Uni et aux États-Unis, le privilège appartient au client et couvre largement les avis des juristes internes ; en France, le secret professionnel est attaché à l'avocat, et la protection des avis des juristes d'entreprise est bien plus limitée.

def: A request that an organisation may refuse because it is clearly without merit, abusive or needlessly repeated.

formal.ex: The Company may refuse to act on a request that is [[manifestly unfounded or excessive]], in particular because of its repetitive character.

everyday.ex: It's obviously [[a fishing expedition]] ahead of his tribunal claim, but that alone doesn't let us refuse.
everyday.ex_us: It's obviously [[a fishing expedition]] ahead of his lawsuit, but that alone doesn't let us refuse.

collocations: to bear the burden of proof
note_fr: Le seuil est élevé et la charge de la preuve pèse sur l'employeur : le fait que le salarié prépare un contentieux ne rend pas sa demande abusive. « A fishing expedition » = une demande faite « à l'aveugle » pour trouver des munitions.

def: The making of a decision about a person by a computer system alone, with no meaningful human involvement.

formal.uk: a decision based solely on automated processing
formal.us: a decision based solely on automated processing
formal.ex: No candidate shall be rejected by [[a decision based solely on automated processing]].

everyday.ex: The tool can rank the CVs, but we can't just [[let the software decide]] who gets rejected.
everyday.ex_us: The tool can rank the résumés, but we can't just [[let the software decide]] who gets rejected.

collocations: to keep a human in the loop
note_fr: « Decision-making » est indénombrable ; une décision se « prend » avec « make » ou « take » (UK), « make » (US). Le RGPD reconnaît le droit de ne pas faire l'objet d'une décision produisant des effets significatifs sur la seule base d'un traitement automatisé : prévoyez une intervention humaine réelle. Aux États-Unis, la ville de New York impose un audit de biais pour ces outils de recrutement.

fr: mosaïque de textes fédéraux et d'États (États-Unis)

term.uk: a patchwork of state and federal laws
term.us: a patchwork of state and federal laws

ipa.uk: /ə ˌpætʃwɜːk əv ˌsteɪt ən ˈfed(ə)rəl lɔːz/
ipa.us: /ə ˌpætʃwɜːrk əv ˌsteɪt ən ˈfedərəl lɔːz/

def: The situation in the United States, where privacy is governed by many separate sector-specific and state rules rather than by one general law.

formal.ex: There is [[no comprehensive federal privacy legislation]] in the United States; obligations arise from sector-specific statutes and from state law.

everyday.uk: it varies from state to state
everyday.us: it varies from state to state
everyday.ex: There's no American GDPR. [[It varies from state to state]], and California goes furthest.

note_fr: À expliquer dans l'autre sens à un client français : pas de texte général, mais des lois sectorielles (santé, rapports d'antécédents, communications électroniques) et des lois d'État. La Californie applique sa loi sur la vie privée aux salariés et aux candidats ; la plupart des autres États les en excluent.

def: A formal order from the regulator requiring an organisation to put an end to a breach of the law within a set time.

formal.ex: The authority served the company with a [[formal notice to comply]] within three months.

everyday.ex: They weren't fined, but they [[were ordered to]] switch the cameras off.

collocations: to serve a notice on a company
note_fr: « Mise en demeure » n'a pas d'équivalent unique : « formal notice » pour décrire la procédure de la CNIL, « enforcement notice » pour l'ICO. La CNIL peut rendre publiques ses mises en demeure et ses sanctions (« to name and shame »), ce que les entreprises redoutent souvent plus que l'amende.

def: The duty of an organisation not only to comply with data protection law but to be able to prove that it does.

formal.ex: The controller shall be responsible for, and be able to [[demonstrate compliance]] with, the principles set out above.

everyday.ex: It's not enough to do the right thing; we need [[a paper trail]] showing we did.

informal.ex: Write the reasoning down, if only to [[cover ourselves]].

collocations: to be able to show one's working
note_fr: « Accountability » n'a pas de traduction française satisfaisante : c'est l'obligation de rendre des comptes, plus exigeante que « responsibility ». Construction : « accountable to someone for something ».

fr: protection des données dès la conception et par défaut

term.uk: data protection by design and by default
term.us: data protection by design and by default

ipa.uk: /ˌdeɪtə prəˈtekʃ(ə)n baɪ dɪˈzaɪn ən baɪ dɪˈfɔːlt/
ipa.us: /ˌdeɪtə prəˈtekʃ(ə)n baɪ dɪˈzaɪn ən baɪ dɪˈfɔːlt/

def: The requirement to build privacy safeguards into a system from the outset, and to set it up so that only the necessary data is collected unless someone chooses otherwise.

formal.ex: The Supplier warrants that the platform has been developed in accordance with the principle of data protection [[by design and by default]].

everyday.uk: to build something in from the start
everyday.us: to build something in from the start
everyday.ex: It's far cheaper to [[build privacy in from the start]] than to bolt it on afterwards.

note_fr: « Par défaut » = « by default » : ici, les réglages d'origine d'un outil. « To bolt on » (ajouter après coup) est l'image habituelle pour ce qu'il faut éviter. À exiger des éditeurs de SIRH dès le cahier des charges.

fr: attente raisonnable en matière de vie privée
def: The degree of privacy a person is entitled to assume in a given setting, used by courts to decide whether an intrusion was lawful.

formal.ex: Employees should have [[no expectation of privacy]] in any material created, stored or sent using Company systems.

everyday.ex: On a company laptop in the US, you really can't [[assume anything is private]].

collocations: to have a reasonable expectation of privacy
to defeat an expectation of privacy
note_fr: Critère américain par excellence : il suffit en général d'une politique écrite pour faire disparaître cette attente. La clause « no expectation of privacy », standard dans les manuels américains, ne peut pas être reprise telle quelle en France ni au Royaume-Uni, où le salarié conserve un droit à la vie privée au travail.

fr: gel des données en vue d'un contentieux
def: An instruction to suspend the normal deletion of documents because they may be needed as evidence in a dispute.

formal.ex: You are required [[to preserve all relevant documents]] until further notice, notwithstanding the Company's retention policy.

everyday.ex: Legal have [[put a hold on]] his mailbox, so nothing gets deleted for now.
everyday.ex_us: Legal has [[put a hold on]] his mailbox, so nothing gets deleted for now.

note_fr: Réflexe américain, lié à la procédure de « discovery » : dès qu'un litige est prévisible, l'entreprise doit geler les documents pertinents, sous peine de sanctions. En Europe, il faut concilier ce gel avec la limitation de la conservation : on le borne aux documents utiles et à la durée du litige.

def: As quickly as can reasonably be expected in the circumstances.

formal.ex: The processor shall notify the controller [[without undue delay]] after becoming aware of a personal data breach.

everyday.ex: Tell the DPO [[as soon as you can]]. Don't wait until you've worked out what happened.

informal.ex: Can you get the list of people affected over to me [[asap]]?

collocations: without undue delay and in any event within
note_fr: Formule du RGPD, à reprendre telle quelle dans les contrats. « Undue » = excessif, injustifié. « In the best delays » est un calque incompréhensible ; « asap » se dit lettre par lettre ou /ˈeɪsæp/.
